_note: Source-of-truth for orchestrator loops. CronCreate durable:true does NOT persist in this managed env (verified 2026-06-12) and there is no headless background execution — loops fire only while a Claude session is open + idle, and must be re-armed each session. Re-arm by passing each entry's cron+prompt to CronCreate at session entry (see docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > Loops). Recurring CronCreate jobs also auto-expire after 7 days.

loops.label: Stabilization (bug-fix before features)
loops.prompt: Stabilization loop tick — BUG-FIX BEFORE FEATURES (operator directive). Do NOT start new feature/ROADMAP feature work. Goal this tick: find bugs, fix at root, code-review, patch to best practices. Steps: (1) Discover (bounded — cap context: read at most the top ~15 TESTING.md pending/S:fail rows, and review the diff in compact form) — run `/builder-test ledger` to sweep docs/goal/TESTING.md pending/S:fail rows in the matching phase, AND run `/code-review` on the current diff / recent changes. (2) For each REAL bug or best-practice finding: dispatch repo-scout to locate -> implementer to fix at root (code + tests in the SAME change) -> test-sync-verifier to gate (pytest + ruff + quality-gate + test-sync). (3) Commit ON GREEN only (fix-complete / TESTING ledger token flipped to passed — no intermediate commits). PAUSE and surface to the operator via AskUserQuestion at: PR creation, any runtime-policy or agent-prompt edit, dashboard-gated items, or anything ambiguous. (4) Stop the tick when no in-scope bugs remain. Route every step per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md. Use python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace. If nothing actionable, report "stabilization: clean this tick".

loops.label: Maintenance (mine orchestrated-agent sessions, propose-only)
loops.attendance: unattended; propose-only, never applies runtime/prompt edits
loops.prompt: Maintenance loop tick — PROPOSE-ONLY. Dispatch the session-maintainer subagent (.claude/agents/session-maintainer.md) to mine the Builder's ORCHESTRATED-agent sessions (project prefixes -tmp-aab-workspaces-*, -tmp-devpulse-*, -tmp-claude-*-aab-workspaces-*) over the last 24h using scripts/mine_sessions.py --errors-only (and builder logs analyze where useful). The miner now sweeps nested subagents/ transcripts and reports lane_coverage. COVERAGE GUARD: read lane_coverage + scanned_projects and reconcile against `builder agent sessions --limit 100 --json` — if the builder ran sessions in a lane the miner could not see (codex_sdk writes nothing to ~/.claude/projects), report that as an explicit COVERAGE GAP; never emit a clean 'no blockers' / 'no new sessions' for an unscanned lane. Classify each recurring blocker by root cause into permission / env / tool-schema / sandbox / code-test, with counts and distinct sessions. PROPOSE minimal fixes at the owning surface (execution_policy.py for permission_mode/dontAsk; quality_gates/python_env.py for env; agent-prompt tightening for tool-schema/sandbox), each proposal quoting the VERBATIM current source line (re-read at propose time; no memory anchors) — but do NOT apply any runtime-policy or agent-prompt edit; surface the diffs to the operator for approval. DEDUPE before filing: list open `builder backlog item ... --source validation` and skip signatures already tracked (reference the id) — only file genuinely new findings via `builder backlog item create --source validation` (incident/improvement/optimization) and propose `builder memory add` for new reusable patterns. If coverage is complete and no new blockers, report "maintenance: no new blockers (lanes: <lane_coverage>)" and stop; if a lane was unscanned, report the COVERAGE GAP instead of an all-clear.

loops.label: Hygiene (/self-optimize on dev sessions, propose-only)
loops.prompt: Hygiene loop tick — PROPOSE-ONLY (weekly). Run the /self-optimize skill (clustering lane) over my dev sessions for the last 7 days. Cluster recurring operator corrections into ranked themes, map each to the single owning surface (a .claude/agents/ fleet prompt, AGENTS.md, a skill SKILL.md, or tests/conftest.py), and PROPOSE the targeted edit — do NOT apply without surfacing the ranked findings to the operator first. Append genuinely new durable learnings to project memory (additive only) and update MEMORY.md. Keep it root-cause not symptom; one surface per theme. If no meaningful new corrections this week, report "hygiene: no new themes" and stop.

loops.label: Capability-fit currency (refresh skill + rubrics from live docs, propose-only)
loops.attendance: on-demand only — trigger manually; do NOT arm via CronCreate. Orchestrator-led, propose-only, browser-verified; all writes by the main agent.
loops.prompt: Capability-fit currency — ON-DEMAND, ORCHESTRATOR-LED, PROPOSE-ONLY, BROWSER-VERIFIED. Goal: keep the global advise-only `capability-fit` skill + its rubrics current with Claude Code / Agent SDK docs. capability-fit STAYS advise-only; the MAIN AGENT is the SOLE writer — subagents never write. Pattern: (1) MAIN AGENT — HIGH-LEVEL DISCOVERY FIRST. Read watermark `last_checked_week` in .claude/loops/capfit-currency-state.json (create at current ISO week if absent). Drive /hermes-chrome YOURSELF (rendered DOM, NEVER WebFetch — it hallucinates doc facts, proven 2026-06-16). (a) CHANGELOG-FIRST: open code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog and walk version entries DOWN to the watermark date; extract every NEW or CHANGED capability — this is the highest-yield surface, most deltas live here, and NEW capabilities (not just changed facts) count. (b) TRAVERSE THE WHOLE HEADER BAR: the docs have multiple top header tabs (e.g. Configuration / Reference / Agent SDK / What's New / Resources) and EACH tab swaps in its OWN sidebar — sweep every tab's sidebar, do NOT stop at the first. The Agent SDK header tab backs claude-agent-sdk-rubric; the Claude Code tabs back claude-code-rubric; Codex is a SEPARATE docs site (openai/codex) backing codex-sdk-rubric (its own pass). (c) SURFACE→RUBRIC GAP RULE: diff live capabilities against each rubric's existing rows — a capability present in the docs but ABSENT from the rubric is a new-coverage gap to ADD, not only changed facts to fix; also flag structural defects (e.g. duplicate sections) for dedup. No changes anywhere -> report "capfit: no doc changes" and stop. Produce a bounded list of changed/new/missing surfaces + the rubric each maps to. (2) MAIN AGENT — SPAWN ONE READ-ONLY SUBAGENT PER CHANGED SURFACE, each given exactly: BOUNDARY (one doc page/section/capability to verify, nothing else); CONTEXT (the precise current claim in capability-fit SKILL.md or the rubric for that capability + the doc URL + the watermark); RETURN CONTRACT (return verbatim rendered-DOM QUOTES + a verdict per item {confirmed | changed→<new fact> | new | removed} — NO summaries, NO proposed edits, NO writes). Each subagent uses its own /hermes-chrome sessionName (concurrency-safe). Subagents VERIFY ONLY and return to the main agent. (3) MAIN AGENT — collate the subagents' quotes+verdicts; draft the minimal patch per verified change to the OWNING surface only: capability-fit `SKILL.md` facts (model tiers, effort levels incl. availability, frontmatter field list, isolation/fork) and/or the shared-KB rubric articles in ~/.claude/knowledge/raw/ (claude-code-rubric, claude-agent-sdk-rubric, codex-sdk-rubric, capability-cost-efficiency-map). Bounded: ONLY those surfaces — never an audited artifact, never unrelated files. (4) MAIN AGENT — PROPOSE the delta + diffs via AskUserQuestion; do NOT auto-apply. On approval, the MAIN AGENT performs ALL edits (sole writer), commits to ~/.claude (uncommitted config is reverted by the cross-machine sync), does NOT push unless told, and bumps `last_checked_week`. Every asserted fact MUST trace to a subagent's rendered-DOM quote, never a WebFetch summary. Use python3 not python; argv-style Bash.

loops.label: Optimization (autonomously advance one efficiency/cost IMP end-to-end to a propose-at-PR gate)
loops.attendance: on-demand only — trigger manually; do NOT arm via CronCreate (it builds features = high-cost, must be attended). Orchestrator-led; autonomous through SELECT+BUILD+VERIFY+VALIDATE; STOPS at an operator approval gate (propose-at-PR). Never auto-merges or pushes to master unattended.
loops.prompt: Optimization loop tick — ON-DEMAND, ORCHESTRATOR-LED, ATTENDED, PROPOSE-AT-PR (never auto-merge or push to master). Goal: autonomously advance ONE efficiency/cost-optimization ROADMAP item end-to-end, stopping at an operator approval gate. Steps: (1) SELECT (bounded) — read docs/goal/ROADMAP.md; from the OPEN `[ ]` items pick the single highest-leverage EFFICIENCY/COST/TOKEN optimization item (e.g. IMP-028 code-gen context replay ~89% of run cost; IMP-027 complexity-proportional SDLC; G13 effort carve-out; G14 OTel). Prefer the largest stated cost leverage that is not blocked. If a prior tick left an in-flight optimization branch, RESUME it instead of starting new. If no open optimization item, report "optimization: none open" and stop. Do NOT touch non-efficiency features (those belong to the stabilization/feature lanes). (2) BUILD (isolated) — create an isolated git worktree/branch, NEVER build on master (see docs/workflows/git-worktree-best-practices). Dispatch planner (architect the change: owner-surface checks, test-sync, risks) -> implementer (code + tests in the SAME change). Keep changes bounded to the selected item; cross an owner boundary only if the plan requires it and call it out. (3) VERIFY correctness — dispatch test-sync-verifier (pytest + ruff + the touched builder quality-gate + test-sync grep). If the change touches frontend/ or the embedded dashboard, ALSO dispatch browser-verifier for live proof. Correctness MUST be green before proceeding; if red, route back to implementer to fix at root (bounded retries), else stop and surface the blocker. (4) VALIDATE the saving — it is an optimization, so PROVE it saves. If autoresearch is ACTIVE (docs/autoresearch/baseline_runs.tsv is non-empty), run the autoresearch Iterate lane (/autoresearch -> Iterate) on the relevant fixture(s): the saving MUST clear the 2-sigma baseline floor with NO gate_pass_rate regression to count as VALIDATED. If autoresearch is still ACTIVATING (baseline empty), do NOT block — capture a saving ESTIMATE via `builder logs analyze --session <id>` (token/cost delta, now accurate post-IMP-023) on a before/after run, and FLAG the proposal "saving ESTIMATED — statistical validation PENDING autoresearch baseline; run /autoresearch Baseline to enable". NEVER claim a validated saving without the 2-sigma evidence. (5) PROPOSE-AT-PR gate — STOP. Commit ON GREEN to the isolated branch ONLY (no push to master, no auto-merge). Surface to the operator via AskUserQuestion an evidence bundle: which IMP, diff summary, correctness result, and the saving (validated 2-sigma delta OR estimate + pending-flag). On approval, open the PR (gh) / push the branch; on hold, leave the branch intact for the next tick to RESUME. NEVER merge or push to master unattended. Route every step per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md. Use python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace; the main thread owns commits/PRs and the approval gate.
